help.tips[0].examples[0].en: The crying woman sat next to the sleeping dog.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Rising prices are worrying many families.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: Active and happening now = Partizip I (spielend), and after die in the plural the adjective ending is -en.
help.tips[0].en.text: lachen → lachend → das lachende Kind · schlafen → schlafend → der schlafende Hund · spielen → die spielenden Kinder · fahren → der fahrende Zug. = das Kind, das (gerade) lacht.
help.tips[0].en.title: Partizip I = infinitive + d + ending (active, now)
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: The letter written yesterday lies on the repaired printer.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Unfortunately we had to cancel the planned trip.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: Already done to the shoes = Partizip II (gekauft), plus the plural ending -en after die.
help.tips[1].en.text: öffnen → geöffnet → die geöffnete Tür · kaufen → das gekaufte Auto · schreiben → der geschriebene Brief · verlieren → die verlorenen Schlüssel. = die Tür, die geöffnet wurde / ist.
help.tips[1].en.title: Partizip II + ending (passive / completed)
help.tips[1].en.trap: the participle is an adjective here, so it must carry the adjective ending: die geöffnete Tür, not die geöffnet Tür.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: Careful, boiling water! — Drink only boiled water.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: Never jump onto a moving train! — The kilometres driven are in the logbook.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: Boiling right now is active: kochend. After das (neuter accusative) the ending is -e.
help.tips[2].en.text: das kochende Wasser (boiling, active, now) — das gekochte Wasser (boiled, done). der fahrende Zug (moving) — der gefahrene Weg (travelled). Ask: is it doing, or has it been done?
help.tips[2].en.title: kochend vs gekocht — the pair that shows the rule
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: 'lost' works like English -ed = Partizip II verloren, and after den (masculine accusative) it needs -en.
help.tips[3].en.text: lachend = laughing, gekauft = bought. The mapping is almost perfect — just add the German adjective ending.
help.tips[3].en.title: -end = English -ing; ge- = English -ed
help.context.en: In the waiting room: a sleeping man, a crying baby, a woman reading. On the table lie old magazines and a forgotten umbrella. Through the opened door you can hear the ringing telephones. And on the wall hangs a handwritten note: "The medicines you ordered can be collected at reception."
help.mistakes[1].whyEn: Partizip I has no ge-; choose active (-end) or passive (ge-).
help.hookEn: Turn 'the child who is laughing' into das lachende Kind — the compact two-word style of written German.
help.introEn: Both participles can stand before a noun as adjectives, and they then take ordinary adjective endings. Partizip I (infinitive + -d: lachend, schlafend, kochend) describes something happening right now, actively: das lachende Kind (the laughing child), der schlafende Hund, das kochende Wasser (the boiling water). Partizip II (the ge- form) describes something done or finished, usually passively: die geöffnete Tür (the opened door), das gekochte Wasser (the boiled water), der geschriebene Brief, die verlorenen Schlüssel. The pair kochend / gekocht shows the difference exactly: boiling versus boiled. Both replace a relative clause — das Kind, das lacht → das lachende Kind; die Tür, die geöffnet wurde → die geöffnete Tür — which is why written German, which likes compact noun phrases, uses them constantly. This is an intro; later modules consolidate it and extend the phrase (das gestern von mir geschriebene …). The quiz gives only the verb; the English line tells you whether the meaning is active and ongoing (-end) or done (ge-…-t / -en) — boiling water or boiled water — and you add the ending the article and case require.
help.rememberEn[0]: -end + ending = happening now; ge-…-t/-en + ending = done.
help.rememberEn[1]: Both are adjectives: same endings as groß, alt, neu.
sentences[0].whyEn: In the act (active): Partizip I = infinitive + d — lachend + -e.
sentences[1].whyEn: It is boiling NOW: kochend + -es (neuter, no article).
sentences[3].whyEn: He is sleeping right now: schlafend + -e.
sentences[4].whyEn: The door HAS BEEN opened (state): geöffnet + -e.
sentences[10].whyEn: She is crying as she does: weinend + -e.
sentences[15].whyEn: The voice trembles as she speaks: zitternd + dative feminine -er.
